result.summary: The page is largely well-designed and functional. The main visual problem is horizontal clipping of the third card in the 'Fastest near you' carousel ('Trattoria Piccol...'), where the restaurant name is truncated mid-word without a clear visual affordance that the row is scrollable. Other findings are minor cosmetic/accessibility notes.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' horizontal carousel, the third card ('Trattoria Piccol...') is cut off at the right edge and its title is truncated mid-word. There is no visible scroll indicator, gradient fade, or partial-card hint that clearly communicates the row is horizontally scrollable, which can make the layout look broken rather than intentional.
issues.suggestion: Add a right-edge fade/gradient or peek of the next card plus a subtle scroll indicator, and ensure card titles truncate with an ellipsis at a consistent breakpoint so clipped cards still look intentional.

issues.description: The notification bell icon in the top-right relies only on a small red dot to convey unread notifications, with no text label or badge count, which is hard to perceive for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible label (e.g. aria-label 'Notifications, 1 unread') and consider a numeric badge or stronger visual cue in addition to the color-only dot.

issues.description: The category filter chips row ('All', 'Pizza', 'Sushi', ...) is also horizontally clipped at the right edge with a partially visible chip, but like the card carousel it lacks a clear scroll affordance.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same horizontal-scroll treatment (edge fade or peek) used elsewhere so the clipped chip reads as scrollable content rather than a layout error.
